column1: # How each failing case of the computed-value gate (tools/conformance/css_computed_suite.py) is listed. tools/conformance/classify-computed.py reads this table and the
# failures the gate reports, and writes CSS_COMPUTED_EXCEPTIONS and CSS_COMPUTED_DEFECTS; a failure no row matches is an error, and so is a row no failure matches.
#   <property regex> TAB <answer regex> TAB <kind> TAB <class or owner> TAB <reason or what the library lacks>
# The property regex is matched in full against the property (the page's, dashed); the answer regex is searched in what the library answered (".*" for any). kind is
# `exception` (the class is one of tools/conformance/css_computed_suite.py's) or `defect` (the owner is the piece of work that closes it). The first row that matches wins.
# Served text quoted for resolved-value (CSSOM, "Resolved Values", drafts.csswg.org/cssom, served 2026-10-27): "The resolved value is the computed value." for any other
# property, and for the properties that have a special case: "then the resolved value is the used value." (the size, margin, padding and inset properties, the colors
# that are `currentcolor`, line-height, the grid track lists, transform-origin and perspective-origin's percentages: a value that depends on layout).

column5: the track list of a grid container resolves to the used track sizes, and to `none` where the element is not a grid container: "then the resolved value is the used value."
a percentage resolves against the box (the 200 by 300 pixel box of the page): "then the resolved value is the used value."
a percentage or a calculation with one resolves to the used length: "then the resolved value is the used value."
the size of a box resolves to its used size: "then the resolved value is the used value."
a number resolves to the used length: "then the resolved value is the used value."

contrast-color(), color-mix(), relative colors and alpha() stay as written for every property (the 7 listed defects of the registered-property gate): a function of colors is not computed to its sRGB form or its simplified arguments
the second value of `caret-color` when it is `auto` is dropped from the computed value (Basic UI 4: the block caret takes the first), and this library keeps it
the lengths of a `clip` rectangle are not made absolute when they are relative or a calculation (`calc(-1em + 10px)` is -30px at a font size of 40px)
a calculation of a percentage and a zero length is not simplified to the percentage (`calc(10% + 0px)` is `10%`)
`currentcolor` resolves to the used color of the element: "then the resolved value is the used value."
the arguments of `sign()` in a ratio are not resolved (a calculation that resolves to a number is a number)
the property is classified unimplemented (the 15 listed in the plan: -webkit-box-*, -webkit-user-select, corner-*-shape, position-area)
`corner-*` and the `corner-*-shape` longhands are unimplemented
unimplemented, or the initial value of a newer draft
a calculation of container or font-relative units inside a function argument that the walker does not compute (filter(), contrast-color(), font-feature-settings, counters, ...)
a gradient is not written in its computed form (default position and shape omitted, positions and sizes made absolute, a color stop in sRGB): the image functions are specified values
the arguments of a filter function are not computed (blur() is blur(0px), a percentage amount is a number, calc() is simplified)
a basic shape is not written in its computed form (rect() and xywh() as inset(), `center` as 50%, a ray's angle in degrees)
color-mix(), relative colors, contrast-color() and alpha() stay as written for every property (the 7 listed defects of the registered-property gate)

the computed value of this property is written differently from the page's expectation: a newer draft than the pin, a shortest form, a default that is written, or a computation that is not done (the page's expectation is in the list of the case)
